proposals.risk: Uncalibrated hypothesis: eliminating the defined nitrogen-purge duration could leave oxygen in the reactor, increasing the risk of palladium-catalyst deactivation.
proposals.rationale: This isolates inert-atmosphere conditioning as a potential sensitivity without asserting that catalyst oxidation occurred.

proposals.risk: Uncalibrated hypothesis: replacing cesium carbonate with the existing solvent removes the intended base function and may prevent efficient amine activation for C–N coupling.
proposals.rationale: This is a reagent-identity intervention targeting the base-dependent coupling mechanism while retaining only listed reagents.

proposals.risk: Uncalibrated hypothesis: replacing Pd2(dba)3 with the phosphine ligand removes the palladium source and may suppress the catalytic cycle.
proposals.rationale: This distinguishes the requirement for a palladium precursor from the separately supplied ligand.

proposals.risk: Uncalibrated hypothesis: removing the specified heating setpoint may reduce the thermal driving force and lead to incomplete conversion within the stated reaction time.
proposals.rationale: This targets temperature control as a single operational dependency without introducing an unsupported alternative temperature.

proposals.risk: Uncalibrated hypothesis: deleting the reactor–heater connection may prevent reliable transfer of the programmed heating condition to the reaction vessel.
proposals.rationale: This isolates apparatus thermal coupling as a potential source of insufficient or uncontrolled reaction heating.
